bull.t: Strong cash generation and profitability inflection
bull.b: Consistent operating cash flow and positive free cash flow provide durable funding for investments, absorb cyclical volatility, and reduce reliance on external capital. Profitability inflection shows scalable unit economics that support reinvestment in growth and margin expansion over multiple quarters.

Multiple revenue streams—marketplace take-rates, subscriptions, advertising, logistics and new verticals—reduce dependency on any single channel. Ads and subscriptions scale with engagement, improving per-order economics and supporting margin sustainability as order volumes mature across geographies.

Focused tech replatforming and AI-driven productivity create lasting operating leverage by raising engineering velocity, reducing time-to-market, and lowering per-feature costs. These structural upgrades should improve long-term unit economics and enable faster rollouts across new verticals and geographies.

bear.t: Rising total debt vs prior years
bear.b: An increase in absolute debt raises refinancing and flexibility risks if growth or margins reaccelerate more slowly than planned. Even with moderate leverage today, higher debt reduces capacity for opportunistic investments and heightens sensitivity to cash-flow shortfalls over the coming quarters.

Running parallel platforms creates persistent incremental OpEx and execution complexity that can depress margins until consolidation completes. Prolonged redundancy consumes cash and management focus, risking missed efficiency targets and delaying the full realization of projected tech productivity gains.

Scaling grocery requires tight inventory, accuracy and fulfillment systems; current gaps limit customer satisfaction and basket economics. Persistent operational shortfalls could cap market share gains and force further investment to reach sustainable unit economics across a capital- and operations-intensive segment.
